claims.source: The number of DTEGs in each knock-down correlated well with the severity of the overall phenotype and with the impact on global translation, as judged from the polysome profiles.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on comparing DTEG counts with polysome profile data.

claims.claim: Only 1045 DTEGs are unique for eIF3dKD and the rest (926) are shared with other two knock-downs.
claims.source: Interestingly, there is a considerable overlap between the knock-downs studied, such that only 1045 DTEGs are unique for eIF3dKD and the rest (926) are shared with other two knock-downs; in particular 923 with eIF3eKD and 21 with eIF3hKD – in the latter case, the overlap reaches 100% (Figure 2F, Figure 2—figure supplement 4A–C).
claims.evidence: This is supported by Venn diagram analysis shown in Figure 2F.

claims.claim: 923 DTEGs are shared between eIF3dKD and eIF3eKD.
claims.source: Interestingly, there is a considerable overlap between the knock-downs studied, such that only 1045 DTEGs are unique for eIF3dKD and the rest (926) are shared with other two knock-downs; in particular 923 with eIF3eKD and 21 with eIF3hKD – in the latter case, the overlap reaches 100% (Figure 2F, Figure 2—figure supplement 4A–C).
claims.evidence: This is supported by Venn diagram analysis shown in Figure 2F.

claims.claim: All 21 DTEGs identified in eIF3hKD are also found in eIF3dKD.
claims.source: Interestingly, there is a considerable overlap between the knock-downs studied, such that only 1045 DTEGs are unique for eIF3dKD and the rest (926) are shared with other two knock-downs; in particular 923 with eIF3eKD and 21 with eIF3hKD – in the latter case, the overlap reaches 100% (Figure 2F, Figure 2—figure supplement 4A–C).
claims.evidence: This is supported by Venn diagram analysis shown in Figure 2F.

claims.claim: Only 257 DTEGs are unique to eIF3eKD and the rest (923) are shared with eIF3dKD.
claims.source: In case of eIF3eKD, only 257 DTEGs are unique and the rest (923) are shared with eIF3dKD, 18 of which are also shared with eIF3hKD (Figure 2F, Figure 2—figure supplement 4A–C).
claims.evidence: This is supported by Venn diagram analysis shown in Figure 2F.

claims.claim: The eIF3 subcomplex formed in eIF3eKD lacks subunits e, k and l and partially also eIF3d.
claims.source: The eIF3 subcomplex formed in eIF3eKD lacks subunits e, k and l and partially also eIF3d (Wagner et al., 2016) – the significantly reduced protein levels of eIF3d are evident in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.
claims.evidence: This is supported by citation to Wagner et al., 2016 and western blot data in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claims.claim: DTEGs upregulated in eIF3dKD and eIF3eKD showed strongest enrichment in the KEGG 'Lysosome' and 'Protein processing in endoplasmic reticulum' pathways.
claims.source: Analysis of DTEGs upregulated in eIF3dKD and eIF3eKD showed similar results for almost all groups analyzed (eIF3dKD 'all', 'unique', and 'translation only', eIF3dKD/eIF3eKD 'common', as well as eIF3eKD 'all' and 'translation only'; Figure 3A, B, and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A), with the strongest enrichment in the KEGG 'Lysosome' and 'Protein processing in endoplasmic reticulum' pathways.
claims.evidence: This is supported by KEGG enrichment analysis shown in Figure 3A, B, and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claims.claim: More than 70% of DTEGs in the KEGG pathway 'Lysosome' upregulated in eIF3dKD fall into the 'translation only' group.
claims.source: For example, for the KEGG pathway 'Lysosome', more than 70% (i.e. 37 out of the 51) DTEGs upregulated in the eIF3dKD 'all', fall into the eIF3dKD 'translation only' group.
claims.evidence: This is based on analysis of the KEGG enrichment data.

claims.claim: Lin et al. detected increased lysosomal load in MCF-10A cells downregulated for eIF3e.
claims.source: Interestingly and in accord with our results, Lin et al. detected increased lysosomal load in MCF-10A cells downregulated for eIF3e (Lin et al., 2020).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citation to Lin et al., 2020.

claims.claim: eIF3e seems to be primarily involved in controlling the balanced production of mature ribosomes.
claims.source: Based on our analysis, eIF3e seems to be primarily involved in controlling the balanced production of mature ribosomes, as its loss resulted in significant number of 'unique upregulated' DTEGs with strong enrichment for the KEGG Ribosome and GO Translation and Ribosome biogenesis terms (Figure 3C and Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
claims.evidence: This is inferred from KEGG and GO enrichment analysis shown in Figure 3C and Figure 3—figure supplement 1B.

claims.claim: 32 ribosomal proteins with significantly changed TE were identified in eIF3eKD (14 cytoplasmic and 18 mitochondrial).
claims.source: In total, we identified 32 RPs with significantly changed TE in eIF3eKD (14 cytoplasmic and 18 mitochondrial) and only 16 in eIF3dKD (9 cytoplasmic and 7 mitochondrial).
claims.evidence: This is a direct result from analyzing ribosomal proteins in the differential expression data.

claims.claim: 16 ribosomal proteins with significantly changed TE were identified in eIF3dKD (9 cytoplasmic and 7 mitochondrial).
claims.source: In total, we identified 32 RPs with significantly changed TE in eIF3eKD (14 cytoplasmic and 18 mitochondrial) and only 16 in eIF3dKD (9 cytoplasmic and 7 mitochondrial).
claims.evidence: This is a direct result from analyzing ribosomal proteins in the differential expression data.

claims.claim: All cytoplasmic ribosomal proteins with increased TE in eIF3eKD were upregulated solely at the translational level.
claims.source: Moreover, all the cytoplasmic RPs with increased TE in eIF3eKD (and most mitochondrial ones) were upregulated solely at the translational level and their mRNA levels were not changed.
claims.evidence: This is based on analysis of the differential expression data for ribosomal proteins.

claims.claim: All ribosomal proteins tested by western blotting showed visibly increased protein levels in both eIF3eKD and eIF3dKD.
claims.source: All ribosomal proteins tested showed visibly increased protein levels in both eIF3eKD and eIF3dKD (Figure 3E, F), while their mRNA levels remained unchanged (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
claims.evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 3E, F and qPCR data in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C.

claims.claim: The 60S/40S subunit ratio remained unaffected in all three knock-downs.
claims.source: We performed polysome profiling in the presence of EDTA that splits all ribosomes into 40 S and 60 S subunits and showed that the 60 S/40 S ratio remained unaffected (Figure 3G).
claims.evidence: This is supported by polysome profiling data shown in Figure 3G.

claims.claim: The total amount of ribosomes in cells is increased in eIF3eKD and eIF3dKD.
claims.source: Furthermore, we performed a similar experiment with exactly 10 million cells per each sample and confirmed that the total amount of ribosomes in cells is indeed increased in eIF3eKD and eIF3dKD (Figure 3H).
claims.evidence: This is supported by ribosome content analysis shown in Figure 3H.

claims.claim: Targeting eIF3e with siRNA results in co-downregulation of eIF3e, eIF3d, eIF3k and eIF3l.
claims.source: As mentioned above, targeting eIF3e with siRNA results in co-downregulation of not only eIF3e and eIF3d, but also of eIF3k and eIF3l (Wagner et al., 2016) which may at least partially explain these findings.
claims.evidence: This is supported by citation to Wagner et al., 2016.

claims.claim: Cells depleted of eIF3k showed increased ribosomal content.
claims.source: A similar role has recently been attributed to eIF3k, which has been shown to specifically repress the synthesis of the small ribosomal protein RPS15A, and cells depleted of eIF3k showed increased ribosomal content (Duan et al., 2023).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citation to Duan et al., 2023.

claims.claim: Transcripts harboring TOP motifs were significantly translationally activated in eIF3dKD and eIF3eKD, but not in eIF3hKD.
claims.source: We observed that transcripts harboring TOP motifs (Philippe et al., 2020) were significantly translationally activated in eIF3dKD and eIF3eKD, but not in eIF3hKD (Figure 4A–C).
claims.evidence: This is supported by analysis of TOP mRNAs shown in Figure 4A–C.

claims.claim: Non-TOP mTORC1-sensitive transcripts were predominantly translationally offset (buffered) in eIF3dKD and eIF3eKD.
claims.source: Interestingly, the effect of eIF3dKD and eIF3eKD on translation of non-TOP mRNAs that are mTORC1-sensitive (Gandin et al., 2016) differed from what was observed for TOP mRNAs, as non-TOP transcripts were predominantly translationally offset (buffered), such that translation efficiency was increased to maintain a constant level of polysome association despite decreased total mRNA abundance (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A–C).
claims.evidence: This is supported by analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A–C.

claims.claim: eIF3e and eIF3d may play a role in tempering translation of TOP mRNAs under normal cellular conditions.
claims.source: Together, these findings suggest that eIF3e and eIF3d may play a role in tempering translation of TOP mRNAs under normal cellular conditions, and that the loss of these eIF3 subunits has distinct impact on the translatome as compared to mTORC1.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the analysis of TOP mRNA translation in the knock-downs.

claims.claim: Depletion of eIF3d affected multiple components of the MAPK signaling pathways including Grb2, Sos, c-Raf, MEK1, Erk2, MNK1, Rsk2, and CREB.
claims.source: Depletion of eIF3d affected multiple components of the MAPK signaling pathways, which plays a critical role in the regulation of cell proliferation (Zhang and Liu, 2002) and cancer development and progression (reviewed in Dhillon et al., 2007). These include the docking protein Grb2 (encoded by GRB2) and guanine nucleotide exchange factor Sos (SOS1), through kinases c-Raf (RAF1), MEK1 (MAP2K1), Erk2 (MAPK1), MNK1 (MKNK1), Rsk2 (RPS6KA3), to the transcription factor CREB (ATF4).
claims.evidence: This is supported by the differential expression analysis and KEGG pathway enrichment.

claims.claim: Rac1 and PAK1, that activate c-Raf by increasing phosphorylation of Ser338, were significantly affected by eIF3d depletion.
claims.source: In addition, Rac1 and PAK1, that activate c-Raf by increasing phosphorylation of Ser338 (King et al., 1998) were also significantly affected (Figure 1A, Figure 5—figure supplement 1C and Supplementary file 1).
claims.evidence: This is supported by the differential expression data and citation to King et al., 1998.

claims.claim: mRNAs that critically depend on phospho-eIF4E levels were translationally offset in eIF3dKD and eIF3eKD cells.
claims.source: Consistent with the observed translational suppression of MNK1, which phosphorylates eIF4E (Waskiewicz et al., 1997), mRNAs that critically depend on phospho-eIF4E levels (Karampelias et al., 2022) were translationally offset in eIF3dKD and eIF3eKD cells, such that translation efficiency was decreased to maintain a constant level of polysome association despite increased total mRNA abundance (Figure 5—figure supplement 2A, B).
claims.evidence: This is supported by analysis shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2A, B and citations.

claims.claim: More than half (26 of the 42) downregulated DTEGs belonging to the 'MAPK signaling pathway' can be classified as translationally buffered.
claims.source: Interestingly, more than half (26 of the 42) downregulated DTEGs belonging to the 'MAPK signaling pathway' can be classified as translationally buffered; that is, their mRNA levels increase while their TE decreases (Kusnadi et al., 2022).
claims.evidence: This is based on analysis of the differential expression data for MAPK pathway genes.

claims.claim: AKT1, GRB2, MAP2K1 (MEK1), PAK1, RPS6KA1 (RSK1), RPS6KA3 (RSK2), RAF1 and SOS1 had visibly decreased protein levels in eIF3dKD and most of them also in eIF3eKD.
claims.source: We found, that AKT1, GRB2, MAP2K1 (MEK1), PAK1, RPS6KA1 (RSK1), RPS6KA3 (RSK2), RAF1 and SOS1 had visibly decreased protein levels in eIF3dKD and most of them also in eIF3eKD.
claims.evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 5C, D.

claims.claim: The transcription factor c-Jun showed increased mRNA and FP levels, unchanged TE, but robust increases in protein levels in all three knock-downs.
claims.source: An interesting exception is the transcription factor c-Jun, which showed increased mRNA and FP levels, unchanged TE, but robust increases in protein levels in all three knock-downs (Figure 5C, D).
claims.evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 5C, D.

claims.claim: ERK1/2 phosphorylation at activation sites Thr202/Tyr204 was increased in all three knock-downs.
claims.source: As with other MAPK proteins, ERK1/2 expression was reduced in eIF3dKD and eIF3eKD, but its phosphorylation at activation sites Thr202/Tyr204 was unexpectedly increased in all three knock-downs (Figure 5E).
claims.evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 5E.

claims.claim: c-Jun was found to be activated by phosphorylation at Ser63 and largely accumulated in the nucleus in all three knock-downs.
claims.source: In accord with increased ERK1/2 phosphorylation, c-Jun was found to be activated by phosphorylation at Ser63 and largely accumulated in the nucleus (Figure 5F).
claims.evidence: This is supported by western blot data of nuclear and cytoplasmic fractions shown in Figure 5F.

claims.claim: MAPK/ERK signaling appears to be activated when eIF3 function in translation is compromised.
claims.source: Thus, despite reduced MAPK/ERK pathway protein levels, MAPK/ERK signaling appears to be activated when eIF3 function in translation is compromised.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the increased ERK1/2 and c-Jun phosphorylation data.

claims.claim: Knocking down eIF3h generates an eIF3 subcomplex lacking eIF3h and two nonessential subunits eIF3k and eIF3l.
claims.source: Knocking down eIF3h generates an eIF3 subcomplex lacking eIF3h and two nonessential subunits eIF3k and eIF3l (Figure 1B), having only negligible impact on overall translation.
claims.evidence: This is supported by Figure 1B and prior research.

claims.claim: 19 transcripts had decreased TE and only 2 transcripts had increased TE in eIF3hKD compared to the NT control.
claims.source: Accordingly, we identified 19 transcripts whose TE was decreased and only 2 transcripts whose TE was increased compared to the NT control (Figure 2D).
claims.evidence: This is a direct result from the differential expression analysis shown in Figure 2D.

claims.claim: MDM2 and ATF4 were common hits in pathways enriched for eIF3hKD downregulated DTEGs.
claims.source: Given the low number of DTEGs, we observed no significant enrichment of any KEGG pathway within the upregulated DTEGs and only a few significant enrichments for the eIF3hKD 'all downregulated' DTEGs in pathways like 'Prostate cancer', 'Viral carcinogenesis' or 'PI3-Akt signaling pathway', all of which included only two common hits – MDM2 and ATF4 (Figure 6A, Supplementary file 2A).
claims.evidence: This is supported by KEGG enrichment analysis shown in Figure 6A.

claims.claim: MDM2 protein levels were reduced in all three knock-downs.
claims.source: We did confirm that the MDM2 protein levels were reduced in all three knock-downs (Figure 6C).
claims.evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 6C.

claims.claim: ATF4 is among the top 10 most significant DTEGs in all three knock-downs.
claims.source: An equally interesting DTEG is ATF4, which is among the top 10 most significant DTEGs in all three knock-downs (Figure 2B, D).
claims.evidence: This is supported by volcano plots shown in Figure 2B, D.

claims.claim: Stress-mediated ATF4 induction was almost abolished in eIF3dKD and eIF3eKD, and strongly decreased in eIF3hKD.
claims.source: Indeed, stress-mediated ATF4 induction was almost abolished in eIF3dKD and eIF3eKD, and strongly decreased in eIF3hKD (Figure 6D).
claims.evidence: This is supported by western blot data after Thapsigargin treatment shown in Figure 6D.

claims.claim: An intact eIF3 complex is required for proper translational control of ATF4.
claims.source: Overall, these findings further confirm that an intact eIF3 complex is required for proper translational control of ATF4, as we and others have previously suggested (Guan et al., 2017; Hronová et al., 2017; Mukhopadhyay et al., 2023; Shu et al., 2022; Wagner et al., 2020), and as discussed below.
claims.evidence: This is supported by the ATF4 data and multiple citations.

claims.claim: In eIF3dKD and eIF3eKD, a markedly increased accumulation of footprints was observed at the most 5' Start-stop element of ATF4.
claims.source: In the case of ATF4, a markedly increased accumulation of footprints was observed at the most 5' Start-stop (St-st) element, specifically in eIF3dKD and eIF3eKD, while coverage of uORF1 decreased, and so did also the basal level of uORF2 (modestly) and ATF4 (Figure 6E).
claims.evidence: This is supported by footprint coverage analysis shown in Figure 6E.

claims.claim: Both eIF3e and eIF3d are required to clear Start-stop-trapped ribosomes on ATF4 mRNA.
claims.source: This agrees well with our observations that ribosomes are stalled at this St-st element (Rendleman et al., 2023; Wagner et al., 2020) and further suggests that both eIF3e and eIF3d are required to clear these St-st-trapped ribosomes.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the footprint accumulation data and supported by citations.

claims.claim: Footprint coverage was increased specifically for uORF1 of MDM2 in all three knock-downs.
claims.source: Regarding MDM2, footprint coverage was increased specifically for uORF1 in all three knock-downs (Figure 6F), consistent with its several-fold stronger inhibitory role on MDM2 expression compared to uORF2 (Jin et al., 2003), which seems to be magnified in the absence of fully functional eIF3.
claims.evidence: This is supported by footprint coverage analysis shown in Figure 6F and citation to Jin et al., 2003.

claims.claim: eIF3d was shown to mediate mechanism of alternative cap-dependent translation initiation in conjunction with DAP5.
claims.source: Last but not least, eIF3d was shown to mediate mechanism of alternative cap-dependent translation initiation in conjunction with DAP5 (p97/NAT1) (Alard et al., 2023; de la Parra et al., 2018a; Volta et al., 2021) and, importantly, DAP5-dependent mRNAs also frequently contain uORFs (David et al., 2022).
claims.evidence: This is supported by multiple citations.

claims.claim: The effects of depletion of DAP5 on the translatome were comparable to those observed in eIF3d-depleted cells.
claims.source: Consistent with this, the effects of depletion of DAP5 on the translatome were comparable to those observed in eIF3d-depleted cells (Figure 6—figure supplement 2A–C); that is, no changes in mRNA levels and the FP coverage moving in the same direction, either up or down.
claims.evidence: This is supported by analysis shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2A–C.

claims.claim: The DAP5-dependent mechanism may rely upon not only eIF3d but also on the entire eIF3 complex.
claims.source: Since similar effects were also observed with eIF3eKD and eIF3hKD, it seems that the DAP5-dependent mechanism may rely upon not only eIF3d but also on the entire eIF3 complex.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the comparison of DAP5 KD effects with eIF3 subunit KD effects.

claims.claim: In all three knock-downs, the change in TE was negatively correlated with the length of 5' and 3' UTR, and with the presence of uORFs in 5' UTR.
claims.source: Indeed, in all three knock-downs, the change in TE was negatively correlated with the length of 5' and 3' UTR, and with the presence of uORFs in 5' UTR (Spearman correlation, p<1 × 10–45) (Figure 7A).
claims.evidence: This is supported by Spearman correlation analysis shown in Figure 7A.

claims.claim: A significant positive Spearman correlation was found between TE changes and the GC content in the coding region (CDS) and 3' UTRs.
claims.source: Moreover, we found a significant positive Spearman correlation between TE changes and the GC content in the coding region (CDS) and 3' UTRs.
claims.evidence: This is supported by Spearman correlation analysis shown in Figure 7A.

claims.claim: In eIF3dKD and eIF3eKD, mRNAs of downregulated DTEGs had longer 5' UTRs, while upregulated DTEGs possessed shorter 5' UTRs.
claims.source: In accordance with the Spearman correlation, in eIF3dKD and eIF3eKD, mRNAs of downregulated DTEGs had longer 5' UTRs, while upregulated DTEGs possessed shorter 5' UTRs, when compared to mRNAs with unchanged TE.
claims.evidence: This is supported by box plot analysis shown in Figure 7B, C.

claims.claim: mRNAs with increased TE in eIF3dKD and eIF3eKD tend to have more GC-rich 3' UTRs and CDS.
claims.source: In terms of GC content, while we observed little significant difference in GC content in the 5' UTR of eIF3dKD and eIF3eKD, there was a highly significant difference in the CDS and 3' UTR of these knock-downs in both downregulated and upregulated DTEGs, indicating that mRNAs with increased TE tend to have more GC-rich 3' UTRs and, surprisingly, CDS and vice versa.
claims.evidence: This is supported by box plot analysis shown in Figure 7B, C.

claims.claim: The 5' UTRs of 'downregulated translation only' DTEGs have a strong tendency to contain uORFs starting with AUG.
claims.source: We did not identify any specific sequence motif, but expectedly, the 5' UTRs of 'downregulated translation only DTEGs have a strong tendency to contain uORFs starting with AUG (Figure 7D, E).
claims.evidence: This is supported by analysis shown in Figure 7D, E.

claims.claim: The intact eIF3 complex is primarily required for translational control of subset of mRNAs containing short uORFs in their 5' UTR even under normal cellular conditions.
claims.source: These findings suggest that the intact eIF3 complex is primarily required for translational control of subset of mRNAs containing short uORFs in their 5' UTR even under normal cellular conditions, like for example MDM2, ATF4 or RAF1, which is in line with its role in translation reinitiation (Valášek et al., 2017), and further discussed below.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the uORF analysis and supported by citation.

claims.claim: Considerably more DTEGs were identified in eIF3dKD than in eIF3eKD, correlating well with the severity of the growth phenotype of both knock-downs.
claims.source: Interestingly, while DTEGs identified in eIF3dKD and eIF3eKD largely overlapped, considerably more DTEGs were identified in eIF3dKD then in eIF3eKD, correlating well with the severity of the growth phenotype of both knock-downs, with the former being more detrimental despite not affecting eIF3 integrity (Wagner et al., 2016).
claims.evidence: This is inferred from comparing DTEG counts with growth phenotype data and supported by citation.

claims.claim: eIF3d levels were more dramatically reduced in eIF3dKD compared to eIF3eKD.
claims.source: Despite being markedly co-downregulated in eIF3eKD, eIF3d levels were more dramatically reduced in eIF3dKD compared to eIF3eKD, as expected.
claims.evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claims.claim: eIF3d is a peripheral subunit that binds to the head of the 40S subunit mainly via the small ribosomal protein Rps16.
claims.source: Furthermore, eIF3d is a peripheral subunit that binds to the head of the 40 S subunit (mainly via the small ribosomal protein Rps16 Herrmannová et al., 2020) and is connected to the eIF3 octamer not only via eIF3e but also via the eIF3a and c subunits (Bochler et al., 2020).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to Herrmannová et al., 2020 and Bochler et al., 2020.

claims.claim: eIF3d may remain partially operational even in the absence of eIF3e.
claims.source: Therefore, we hypothesize that eIF3d may remain partially operational even in the absence of eIF3e, and therefore the more severe phenotype in eIF3dKD is likely to stem from lower levels of the eIF3d protein compared to eIF3eKD.
claims.evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the structural information and phenotype data.

claims.claim: Phenotypes that are common to eIF3dKD and eIF3eKD are likely a consequence of reduction in eIF3d protein levels.
claims.source: Following this logic, phenotypes that are common to eIF3dKD and eIF3eKD are likely a consequence of reduction in eIF3d protein levels.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the comparison of phenotypes and protein levels.

claims.claim: eIF3d (in the context of entire eIF3) was shown to be regulated by stress-triggered phosphorylation.
claims.source: In support, eIF3d (in the context of entire eIF3) was shown to be regulated by stress-triggered phosphorylation (Lamper et al., 2020) and, together with DAP5, it was shown to promote translation by an alternate cap-dependent (eIF4F-independent) mechanism (de la Parra et al., 2018a; Lee et al., 2016).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to Lamper et al., 2020; de la Parra et al., 2018a; Lee et al., 2016.

claims.claim: Activation of the MAPK/ERK pathway is a general consequence of the compromised eIF3 function.
claims.source: Importantly, since the increased ERK1/2 phosphorylation was observed not only in eIF3dKD and eIF3eKD but also in eIF3hKD, where expression of MAPK pathways proteins is unaffected, we conclude that activation of the MAPK/ERK pathway is a general consequence of the compromised eIF3 function.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the ERK1/2 phosphorylation data across all three knock-downs.

claims.claim: Overexpression of eIF3d led to hypo-phosphorylation of MEK1 and ERK1/2 in HTR-8/SVneo cells.
claims.source: Notably, the eIF3d influence on the MAPK/ERK pathway was previously demonstrated in HTR-8/SVneo cells, where overexpression of eIF3d led to hypo-phosphorylation of MEK1 and ERK1/2, while downregulation had the opposite effect; however, no significant effect on the protein levels of its components was detected in this study (Li et al., 2021).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citation to Li et al., 2021.

claims.claim: JUN mRNA was previously shown to interact directly with eIF3 through a stable stem loop occurring in its 5' UTR.
claims.source: Although JUN mRNA was previously shown to interact directly with eIF3 through a stable stem loop occurring in its 5' UTR, which positively stimulated its translation (Lee et al., 2015), in this study we observed upregulation of the JUN mRNA abundance, whereby the depletion of eIF3d, e, or h had no conspicuous effect on its translational efficiency.
claims.evidence: This is supported by citation to Lee et al., 2015.

claims.claim: eIF3d binds to JUN mRNA with increased affinity during chronic ER stress.
claims.source: This can be explained by a recent report showing that eIF3d binds to JUN mRNA with increased affinity during chronic ER stress, suggesting that eIF3d-dependent translational regulation may be triggered by stress (Mukhopadhyay et al., 2023).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citation to Mukhopadhyay et al., 2023.

claims.claim: When translation is compromised, cells attempt to counteract it by producing more ribosomes and activating MAPK signaling.
claims.source: At the current state of our knowledge, we can only speculate that when translation is compromised, cells attempt to counteract it in two ways: (1) they produce more ribosomes to increase translational rates, and (2) activate MAPK signaling to send pro-growth signals that may ultimately further increase ribosome biogenesis, as further discusses below.
claims.evidence: This is speculation based on the observed data.

claims.claim: Lin et al. identified 240 downregulated and 220 upregulated eIF3eKD-specific DTEGs in MCF-10A cells.
claims.source: Recently, Lin et al. carried out Ribo-seq analysis in MCF-10A cells downregulated for eIF3e (Lin et al., 2020). They identified 240 downregulated and 220 upregulated eIF3eKD-specific DTEGs that overlap very poorly with our DTEGs (data not shown).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citation to Lin et al., 2020.

claims.claim: Lin et al. identified a set of 2683 eIF3e-dependent mRNAs encoding many proteins associated with mitochondrial and membrane functions that showed increased ribosome density between codons 25 and 75 in eIF3eKD.
claims.source: In addition, they identified a set of 2683 eIF3e-dependent mRNAs encoding many proteins associated with mitochondrial and membrane functions that showed increased ribosome density between codons 25 and 75 in eIF3eKD.
claims.evidence: This is supported by citation to Lin et al., 2020.

claims.claim: There is a very significant overlap of 446 genes between the eIF3e-dependent mRNAs from Lin et al. and eIF3dKD 'all upregulated' dataset.
claims.source: Despite this 'accumulation effect' discrepancy, comparing our DTEGs with the Lin et al. eIF3e-dependent data, we found a very significant overlap of 446 genes between the eIF3e-dependent mRNAs and our eIF3dKD 'all upregulated' dataset (p<1 × 10–53), while the overlap with eIF3eKD 'all upregulated' – 251 genes – was surprisingly smaller (p<1 × 10–24).
claims.evidence: This is based on comparison with data from Lin et al., 2020.

claims.claim: KEGG enrichment analysis of eIF3e-dependent mRNAs from Lin et al. revealed the same top 2 KEGG pathways as in eIF3dKD and eIF3eKD 'all upregulated' groups: Lysosome and Protein processing in ER.
claims.source: Moreover, our KEGG enrichment analysis of eIF3e-dependent mRNAs from Lin et al. revealed the same top 2 KEGG pathways (data not shown) as in case of eIF3dKD and eIF3eKD 'all upregulated' groups; that is Lysosome and Protein processing in ER (Figure 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
claims.evidence: This is based on KEGG enrichment analysis of data from Lin et al., 2020.

claims.claim: The discrepancy between Ribo-Seq and Western blot results for ribosomal proteins in eIF3eKD versus eIF3dKD might be explained by the enhanced stabilization of RPs by the compensatory dosage mechanism at the protein level.
claims.source: This discrepancy between our Ribo-Seq and Western blot results in eIF3eKD versus eIF3dKD (Figure 3D vs. E) might be explained by the enhanced stabilization of RPs by the previously described compensatory dosage mechanism at the protein level (Ishikawa, 2021).
claims.evidence: This is speculation supported by citation to Ishikawa, 2021.

claims.claim: Increased RP production was recently reported also for eIF3kKD.
claims.source: Similar effect of increased RPs production was recently reported also for eIF3kKD (Duan et al., 2023).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citation to Duan et al., 2023.

claims.claim: eIF3eKD decreases protein levels of eIF3k and eIF3l.
claims.source: Of note, eIF3eKD also decreases protein levels of eIF3k and eIF3l and thus this RP-specific effect could be at least partially attributed to the loss of eIF3k.
claims.evidence: This is supported by western blot data and prior research.

claims.claim: Increased RP production was observed in eIF3dKD, where eIF3k is normally present, but was not observed in eIF3hKD, where eIF3k and eIF3l are also co-depleted.
claims.source: However, increased RP production was also observed in eIF3dKD, where eIF3k is normally present, but was not observed in eIF3hKD, where eIF3k and eIF3l are also co-depleted.
claims.evidence: This is based on the ribosome content and western blot data.

claims.claim: The eIF3 complex exerts control over RP production.
claims.source: Thus, although it now seems well-established that the eIF3 complex exerts control over RP production, the exact contribution of its individual subunits to this regulation awaits further analysis.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the data presented in the manuscript.

claims.claim: TOP mRNAs contain a polypyrimidine tract in their 5' UTR and are regulated solely at the translational level in response to stress or unfavorable growth conditions through mTORC1 or PI3-kinase pathways.
claims.source: An important hint could be that all cytoplasmic RPs with increased TE in eIF3eKD (and most of mitochondrial RPs) were upregulated solely at the translational level (their mRNA levels did not change), which may well correspond to the fact that RP mRNAs belong to the TOP mRNAs family. These mRNAs contain a polypyrimidine tract in their 5' UTR and were suggested to be regulated solely at the translational level in response to stress or unfavorable growth conditions through mTORC1 or PI3-kinase pathways (Cockman et al., 2020; Philippe et al., 2020; Stolovich et al., 2002).
claims.evidence: This is supported by multiple citations.

claims.claim: eIF3e and eIF3d play a role in repressing translation of TOP mRNAs under normal cellular conditions.
claims.source: Accordingly, we found that TOP transcripts were significantly translationally activated in eIF3dKD and eIF3eKD (Figure 4A–C), suggesting a role of eIF3e and eIF3d in repressing translation of TOP mRNAs under normal cellular conditions.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the TOP mRNA analysis shown in Figure 4A–C.

claims.claim: mTOR does not generally operate via eIF3 and eIF3 does not require mTOR activation to fine tune RP production.
claims.source: Interestingly, since mTOR-activated translation of non-TOP transcripts was predominantly translationally offset (buffered) in eIF3dKD and eIF3eKD cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A–C), it appears that both effects are independent of each other; that is, mTOR does not generally operate via eIF3 and eIF3 does not require mTOR activation to fine tune RP production.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the analysis of mTOR-sensitive transcripts shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A–C.

claims.claim: Upregulation of cytosolic ribosomal proteins has previously been reported in association with the eIF3m downregulation at transcriptional level.
claims.source: It is also noteworthy that upregulation of cytosolic ribosomal proteins has previously been reported in association with the eIF3m downregulation – albeit only at transcriptional level (Smekalova et al., 2020), or with downregulation of eEF2 (Gerashchenko et al., 2020).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to Smekalova et al., 2020 and Gerashchenko et al., 2020.

claims.claim: Out of the 402 transcripts with a putative eIF3 binding sites in their 5' UTRs, 92 and 65 had significantly altered TE in the eIF3dKD and eIF3eKD, respectively.
claims.source: We found that out of the 402 transcripts with a putative eIF3 binding sites in their 5' UTRs, 92 and 65 had significantly altered TE in the eIF3dKD and eIF3eKD, respectively (51 were common for both eIF3dKD and eIF3eKD; Figure 7—figure supplement 1B).
claims.evidence: This is based on cross-referencing with data from Lee et al., 2015 shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1B.

claims.claim: eIF3h and specifically modified eIF3a have been directly shown to modulate resumption of scanning from ATF4's uORF1 for efficient reinitiation downstream.
claims.source: Moreover, eIF3h and specifically modified eIF3a have been directly shown to modulate resumption of scanning from ATF4's uORF1 for efficient reinitiation downstream; that is one of the key steps in the ATF4 translational control (Hronová et al., 2017; Shu et al., 2022).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to Hronová et al., 2017; Shu et al., 2022.

claims.claim: The impact on translation of MDM2 mRNA could indicate that eIF3 is also linked to the key tumor suppressor p53.
claims.source: Interestingly, the impact on translation of MDM2 mRNA could indicate that eIF3 is also linked to the key tumor suppressor p53 (Marine and Lozano, 2010).
claims.evidence: This is speculation based on the MDM2 data and supported by citation to Marine and Lozano, 2010.

claims.claim: PRRC2A was significantly upregulated in all three knock-downs.
claims.source: Among a few upregulated DTEGs in eIF3hKD, we noticed PRRC2A, which was significantly upregulated in all three knock-downs and was recently identified by the Teleman's group as a protein interacting with the translational machinery, including eIF3.
claims.evidence: This is based on the differential expression data.

claims.claim: PRRC2 proteins affected translation initiation by promoting leaky scanning.
claims.source: Interestingly, they found that PRRC2 proteins affected translation initiation by promoting leaky scanning (Bohlen et al., 2023) and that the triple knock-down of all PRRC2 proteins (PRRC2A, PRRC2B, PRRC2C) specifically decreased translation efficiency of mRNAs harboring uORFs in their 5' UTRs, including ATF4 and RAF1 studied also here, similar to our eIF3 knock-downs.
claims.evidence: This is supported by citation to Bohlen et al., 2023.

claims.claim: By increased expression of PRRC2A (and also PRRC2B and PRRC2C in eIF3dKD and eIF3eKD), cells attempt to compensate for ineffective translation of mRNAs with short uORFs.
claims.source: Thus, we speculate that by increased expression of PRRC2A (and also PRRC2B and PRRC2C in eIF3dKD and eIF3eKD), cells attempt to compensate for ineffective translation of mRNAs with short uORFs, which often encode regulatory proteins.
claims.evidence: This is speculation based on the PRRC2 data.

claims.claim: All PRRC2 proteins themselves have a highly translated overlapping-uORF in their 5' UTR.
claims.source: Intriguingly, all PRRC2 proteins themselves have a highly translated overlapping-uORF in their 5' UTR, suggesting that they might be a subject to an autoregulatory mechanism.
claims.evidence: This is an observation from the data with speculation about autoregulation.

claims.claim: eIF3 plays a critical role in translational regulation of specific mRNAs encoding regulatory proteins, very often utilizing uORFs and/or specific secondary structures in their 5' UTRs.
claims.source: Although our results presented here and summarized in Figure 7F are limited to HeLa cells and future work is needed to confirm their universal validity in other cells and tissues, a growing body of evidence suggests that eIF3 plays a critical role in translational regulation of specific mRNAs encoding regulatory proteins, very often utilizing uORFs and/or specific secondary structures in their 5' UTRs.
claims.evidence: This is a general conclusion based on the data presented and broader literature.

claims.claim: Alterations in the eIF3 subunit stoichiometry and/or eIF3 subcomplexes have distinct effects on the translatome.
claims.source: Here, we demonstrate that alterations in the eIF3 subunit stoichiometry and/or eIF3 subcomplexes have distinct effects on the translatome; for example, they affect factors that play a prominent (either positive or negative) role in cancer biology (e.g. MDM2 and cJUN), but the resulting impact is unclear so far.
claims.evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the data presented in the manuscript.

claims.claim: Malignant cells exhibit augmented activity of many components of the translation machinery and are inherently believed to become 'addicted' to elevated protein synthesis.
claims.source: Taking into account that malignant cells exhibit augmented activity of many components of the translation machinery and are inherently believed to become 'addicted' to elevated protein synthesis (Ruggero, 2013; Silvera et al., 2010), this type of research is important because it is increasingly apparent that targeting general components of the canonical translational machinery, such as eIF3, which acts upstream of effector proteins directly involved in tumorigenesis, may hold promise for overcoming the major obstacle associated with intratumor heterogeneity.
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to Ruggero, 2013; Silvera et al., 2010.

claims.claim: Targeting general components of the canonical translational machinery, such as eIF3, may hold promise for overcoming the major obstacle associated with intratumor heterogeneity.
claims.source: Taking into account that malignant cells exhibit augmented activity of many components of the translation machinery and are inherently believed to become 'addicted' to elevated protein synthesis (Ruggero, 2013; Silvera et al., 2010), this type of research is important because it is increasingly apparent that targeting general components of the canonical translational machinery, such as eIF3, which acts upstream of effector proteins directly involved in tumorigenesis, may hold promise for overcoming the major obstacle associated with intratumor heterogeneity.
claims.evidence: This is speculation about therapeutic implications based on the research findings.

results.result: The authors successfully generated three distinct eIF3 subunit knockdowns (eIF3d, eIF3e, eIF3h) in HeLa cells using siRNA, achieving 16-32 fold mRNA reduction and corresponding protein depletion. eIF3eKD resulted in co-depletion of eIF3d, eIF3k, and eIF3l, while eIF3hKD depleted eIF3h, eIF3k, and eIF3l. Both eIF3dKD and eIF3eKD strongly reduced cell proliferation and polysome formation, while eIF3hKD had only moderate effects.
results.evaluation: Claims C37-C43 are well-supported by multiple complementary experimental approaches including qPCR (C40), western blotting (C37, C38, C41), polysome profiling (C42, C43), and growth curves (C39). The data consistently demonstrate successful knockdown with expected phenotypic consequences that align with prior work (Wagner et al., 2016).

results.result: Ribo-seq and RNA-seq libraries were of high quality with expected characteristics. Differential expression analysis identified 21 DTEGs in eIF3hKD, 1180 in eIF3eKD, and 1971 in eIF3dKD. The number of DTEGs correlated with phenotype severity, with eIF3hKD showing the mildest impact on the translatome.
results.evaluation: Claims C44-C51 are supported by comprehensive quality control metrics (read length distribution, 3nt periodicity, CDS enrichment) and PCA/clustering analysis. The differential expression analysis using DESeq2 with padj<0.05 threshold is appropriate, and the correlation between DTEG counts and phenotype severity is logically consistent with polysome and growth data.

results.result: There is substantial overlap in DTEGs between knockdowns: 923 DTEGs are shared between eIF3dKD and eIF3eKD, all 21 eIF3hKD DTEGs are found in eIF3dKD, and only 257 DTEGs are unique to eIF3eKD. The eIF3 subcomplex in eIF3eKD lacks subunits e, k, l and partially eIF3d.
results.evaluation: Claims C52-C56 are supported by Venn diagram analysis (Figure 2F) and western blot data (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C). The overlap patterns are consistent with the known structural relationships between eIF3 subunits and provide internal validation of the experimental approach.

results.result: Upregulated DTEGs in eIF3dKD and eIF3eKD showed strongest enrichment in KEGG 'Lysosome' and 'Protein processing in endoplasmic reticulum' pathways, with >70% being translationally regulated. eIF3e appears primarily involved in controlling balanced ribosome production.
results.evaluation: Claims C57-C60 are supported by KEGG enrichment analysis (Figure 3A-C) and classification of DTEGs into 'translation only' groups. The finding is corroborated by independent work (Lin et al., 2020, C59) showing increased lysosomal load in eIF3e-depleted cells, strengthening the conclusion.

results.result: eIF3eKD resulted in 32 ribosomal proteins with significantly changed TE (vs. 16 in eIF3dKD), with cytoplasmic RPs upregulated solely at the translational level. Western blotting confirmed increased RP protein levels in both knockdowns. The 60S/40S ratio remained balanced, but total ribosome content increased in eIF3eKD and eIF3dKD.
results.evaluation: Claims C61-C66 are supported by Ribo-seq analysis, western blotting (Figure 3E-F), qPCR (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C), and polysome profiling with EDTA (Figure 3G-H). The data consistently demonstrate increased RP production without disrupting ribosome stoichiometry, though the discrepancy between Ribo-seq and western blot results for eIF3eKD vs eIF3dKD requires further investigation (acknowledged in C115).

results.result: TOP mRNAs (encoding ribosomal proteins and translational machinery) were significantly translationally activated in eIF3dKD and eIF3eKD but not eIF3hKD. Non-TOP mTORC1-sensitive transcripts were predominantly translationally buffered. This suggests eIF3e and eIF3d temper TOP mRNA translation under normal conditions independently of mTORC1.
results.evaluation: Claims C69-C71 are supported by ECDF analysis of TOP mRNAs (Figure 4A-C) and mTORC1-sensitive transcripts (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A-C). The differential effects on TOP vs. non-TOP mTORC1-sensitive transcripts provide strong evidence for an mTORC1-independent mechanism, though the molecular basis requires further investigation.

results.result: eIF3dKD affected multiple MAPK pathway components (Grb2, Sos, c-Raf, MEK1, Erk2, MNK1, Rsk2, CREB, Rac1, PAK1) at the translational level. Western blotting confirmed decreased protein levels for most tested proteins (AKT1, GRB2, MEK1, PAK1, RSK1, RSK2, RAF1, SOS1) in eIF3dKD and eIF3eKD. More than half of downregulated MAPK pathway DTEGs were translationally buffered.
results.evaluation: Claims C72-C77 are supported by KEGG enrichment analysis, differential expression data, and western blot validation (Figure 5C-D). The exception of c-Jun (C77) showing increased protein despite unchanged TE is well-documented and adds nuance to the findings. The translational buffering pattern (C75) is appropriately characterized.

results.result: Despite reduced MAPK/ERK pathway protein levels, ERK1/2 phosphorylation at Thr202/Tyr204 was increased in all three knockdowns. c-Jun was activated by phosphorylation at Ser63 and accumulated in the nucleus. This indicates MAPK/ERK pathway activation is a general consequence of compromised eIF3 function.
results.evaluation: Claims C78-C80 and C106 are strongly supported by western blot data (Figure 5E-F) showing increased ERK1/2 and c-Jun phosphorylation across all three knockdowns. The observation that eIF3hKD also shows increased ERK phosphorylation despite unaffected MAPK protein levels (C106) provides compelling evidence that pathway activation is independent of protein level changes and represents a compensatory response.

results.result: MDM2 and ATF4 were identified as key DTEGs downregulated in all three knockdowns. MDM2 protein levels were reduced in all knockdowns. ATF4 is among the top 10 most significant DTEGs, and stress-mediated ATF4 induction was almost abolished in eIF3dKD/eIF3eKD and strongly decreased in eIF3hKD. An intact eIF3 complex is required for proper ATF4 translational control.
results.evaluation: Claims C83-C87 are supported by KEGG enrichment analysis (Figure 6A), western blotting (Figure 6C-D), and volcano plots (Figure 2B, D). The ATF4 stress induction experiment (C86) provides functional validation. The conclusion about intact eIF3 requirement (C87) is well-supported by the data and consistent with prior literature.

results.result: Footprint analysis revealed increased accumulation at the 5' Start-stop element of ATF4 in eIF3dKD/eIF3eKD, suggesting both subunits are required to clear Start-stop-trapped ribosomes. For MDM2, footprint coverage increased specifically at uORF1 in all three knockdowns, consistent with its stronger inhibitory role.
results.evaluation: Claims C88-C90 are supported by footprint coverage analysis (Figure 6E-F). The ATF4 Start-stop accumulation pattern is consistent with prior observations (Rendleman et al., 2023; Wagner et al., 2020), and the MDM2 uORF1 accumulation aligns with known regulatory mechanisms (Jin et al., 2003). The data provide mechanistic insight into eIF3's role in reinitiation.

results.result: Changes in translation efficiency correlated with mRNA features: negative correlation with 5'/3' UTR length and uORF presence (p<1×10⁻⁴⁵), positive correlation with GC content in CDS and 3' UTRs. Downregulated DTEGs had longer 5' UTRs and lower GC content, while upregulated DTEGs had shorter 5' UTRs and higher GC content. Downregulated 'translation only' DTEGs strongly tend to contain AUG-initiated uORFs.
results.evaluation: Claims C94-C99 are supported by Spearman correlation analysis (Figure 7A) with highly significant p-values, box plot analysis (Figure 7B-C), and uORF frequency analysis (Figure 7D-E). The statistical significance is robust, and the findings are internally consistent. The conclusion about eIF3's role in translating uORF-containing mRNAs (C99) is well-supported and aligns with known eIF3 functions in reinitiation.

results.result: More DTEGs were identified in eIF3dKD than eIF3eKD despite eIF3dKD not affecting eIF3 integrity. eIF3d levels were more dramatically reduced in eIF3dKD than eIF3eKD. The authors hypothesize that eIF3d may remain partially operational without eIF3e due to its peripheral location and multiple attachment points to the octamer.
results.evaluation: Claims C100-C102 are supported by DTEG counts, western blot data (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C), and structural information from prior work. However, C103-C104 represent hypotheses rather than demonstrated findings. While the speculation is reasonable given the structural data, alternative explanations (e.g., eIF3d having functions outside the complex, or being a target of signaling pathways) are acknowledged but not tested. Further experiments are needed to distinguish between these possibilities.

results.result: The effects of DAP5 depletion on the translatome were comparable to eIF3d-depleted cells, with similar patterns in FP coverage. Since similar effects were observed with eIF3eKD and eIF3hKD, the DAP5-dependent mechanism may rely on the entire eIF3 complex, not just eIF3d.
results.evaluation: Claims C92-C93 are supported by comparative analysis shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2A-C. The observation that all three eIF3 knockdowns show similar effects to DAP5 KD provides evidence for eIF3 complex involvement beyond just eIF3d, though the molecular details of this interaction require further investigation.

results.result: Comparison with Lin et al. (2020) data showed significant overlap: 446 genes between eIF3e-dependent mRNAs and eIF3dKD upregulated DTEGs (p<1×10⁻⁵³). KEGG enrichment of Lin et al. eIF3e-dependent mRNAs revealed the same top 2 pathways (Lysosome and Protein processing in ER) as the current study.
results.evaluation: Claims C113-C114 are supported by cross-study comparison with appropriate statistical testing. The convergence of findings between independent studies using different cell lines (HeLa vs. MCF-10A) strengthens confidence in the biological significance of the lysosome and ER protein processing pathways, despite methodological differences noted in the discussion.

results.result: Cross-referencing with Lee et al. (2015) data on eIF3-binding mRNAs showed that 92 of 402 transcripts with putative eIF3 binding sites had significantly altered TE in eIF3dKD, and 65 in eIF3eKD (51 common to both).
results.evaluation: Claim C124 is supported by cross-referencing analysis shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1B. The notable overlap between transcripts with eIF3 binding sites and those with altered TE provides validation of the screening approach and suggests direct regulatory relationships, though the overlap is modest (~23% for eIF3dKD).

results.result: PRRC2A was significantly upregulated in all three knockdowns. PRRC2 proteins affect translation initiation by promoting leaky scanning and their depletion decreases TE of uORF-containing mRNAs. The authors speculate that increased PRRC2 expression represents a compensatory mechanism for ineffective translation of uORF-containing mRNAs. All PRRC2 proteins have highly translated overlapping-uORFs, suggesting autoregulation.
results.evaluation: Claim C127 is supported by differential expression data. C128 is supported by citation to Bohlen et al., 2023. However, C129 is explicitly speculative and lacks direct experimental validation. C130 is an observation that leads to speculation about autoregulation without testing. While the hypothesis is plausible, it requires experimental validation through PRRC2 manipulation experiments.

results.result: The introduction provides established background on protein synthesis, translation initiation, eIF3 structure and function, MAPK signaling pathways, and their roles in cancer. This includes the modular assembly of eIF3, interconnected expression of eIF3 subunits, and the regulatory relationships between MAPK pathways and translation.
results.evaluation: Claims C1-C36 represent well-established knowledge in the field, supported by appropriate citations to primary literature and reviews. These background claims provide necessary context for interpreting the experimental results and are not contested findings.

results.result: The authors speculate that when translation is compromised, cells attempt to compensate by (1) producing more ribosomes and (2) activating MAPK signaling. They also speculate that targeting eIF3 may hold promise for overcoming intratumor heterogeneity in cancer therapy.
results.evaluation: Claims C110, C129, and C134 are explicitly speculative and represent hypotheses rather than demonstrated findings. While the speculation is reasonable given the observed data (increased ribosome production and MAPK activation), the proposed compensatory mechanisms and therapeutic implications lack direct experimental validation. These represent important directions for future research but should not be considered established results.

results.result: The authors report that depletion of eIF3d or eIF3e reduces protein levels of multiple MAPK signaling pathway components (including Grb2, Sos, c-Raf, MEK1, Erk2, MNK1, Rsk2, and others), yet paradoxically, MAPK/ERK pathway activity is increased in all three knockdowns (eIF3d, eIF3e, and eIF3h), as evidenced by increased ERK1/2 and c-Jun phosphorylation. The authors conclude that MAPK/ERK pathway activation is a general consequence of compromised eIF3 function.
results.evaluation: Reviewers explicitly acknowledge this finding as a key contribution. Reviewer 2 states the authors 'identify MAPK pathway components as a group of targets coordinately regulated by eIF3 d/e' and notes 'proteins encoding components of MAP kinase cascades are downregulated when subunits of eIF3 are knocked down, but retain elevated levels of activity.' Reviewer 3 similarly confirms 'proteins encoding components of MAP kinase cascades are downregulated...but retain elevated levels of activity.' No concerns are raised about this result.

results.result: The authors report that depletion of eIF3e and eIF3d increases translation of TOP mRNAs encoding ribosomal proteins and other translational machinery components. They show increased translation efficiency of ribosomal proteins (32 in eIF3eKD, 16 in eIF3dKD), validated by western blotting, and demonstrate increased total ribosome content in cells while maintaining balanced 60S/40S ratios. The authors conclude that eIF3e and eIF3d play a role in tempering TOP mRNA translation under normal conditions.
results.evaluation: Reviewers explicitly confirm this finding. Reviewer 1 states 'Their results support and extend previous reports suggesting that both factors control translation of 5'TOP mRNAs.' Reviewer 2 notes 'Both eIF3d/e KD increase translation efficiency (TE) of transcripts encoding lysosomal, ER and ribosomal proteins, suggesting a role of eIF3 in ribosome biogenesis.' Reviewer 3 confirms 'RNAs relying on TOP motifs for translation, such as ribosomal protein RNAs...are upregulated.' No methodological concerns are raised.

results.result: The authors report that alterations in eIF3 subunit stoichiometry are associated with changes in translation of mRNAs containing short uORFs, specifically demonstrating reduced protein levels and altered ribosome footprint patterns for MDM2 and ATF4 in all three knockdowns. They show increased footprint accumulation at specific uORF elements and conclude that an intact eIF3 complex is required for proper translational control of uORF-containing mRNAs.
results.evaluation: Reviewers acknowledge this finding as confirmatory and important. Reviewer 1 states 'The authors confirm prior observations that eIF3...is important for translation re-initiation.' Reviewer 2 notes 'MDM2 and ATF4 both contain short uORFs upstream of the start codon, and further supports a role of eIF3 in reinitiation.' Reviewer 1 notes the authors 'have not...provided additional experimental evidence that uORF-mediated translation of Raf-1 mRNA depends on an intact eIF3 complex' but does not challenge the core findings on MDM2 and ATF4.

results.result: The authors identify 21 DTEGs in eIF3hKD, 1180 DTEGs in eIF3eKD, and 1971 DTEGs in eIF3dKD, with substantial overlap between knockdowns (923 shared between eIF3dKD and eIF3eKD; all 21 eIF3hKD DTEGs found in eIF3dKD). They report that the number of DTEGs correlates with phenotype severity and that eIF3h depletion has much milder impact than eIF3e or eIF3d depletion.
results.evaluation: Reviewers accept these findings without challenge. Reviewer 2 states 'eIF3d/e KD, while translation defects upon eIF3h KD were mild' and 'eIF3d/eKD share multiple dysregulated transcripts.' The editor notes the study 'demonstrates mRNA-specific regulation of translation by subunits of the eukaryotic initiation factor complex 3 (eIF3) using convincing methods, data, and analyses.' No concerns are raised about the differential expression analysis or overlap patterns.

results.result: The authors report that DTEGs upregulated in eIF3dKD and eIF3eKD show strongest enrichment in KEGG 'Lysosome' and 'Protein processing in endoplasmic reticulum' pathways, with more than 70% of lysosomal pathway DTEGs being translationally regulated. They cite concordant findings from Lin et al. showing increased lysosomal load in eIF3e-depleted cells.
results.evaluation: Reviewers acknowledge this finding. Reviewer 2 states 'Both eIF3d/e KD increase translation efficiency (TE) of transcripts encoding lysosomal, ER and ribosomal proteins.' Reviewer 3 notes 'RNAs encoding modification enzymes in the ER and components of the lysosome are upregulated.' No concerns are raised about the pathway enrichment analysis or interpretation.

results.result: The authors characterize the eIF3 subcomplexes formed by siRNA knockdown: eIF3e depletion reduces eIF3e, eIF3d, eIF3k, and eIF3l; eIF3h depletion reduces eIF3h, eIF3k, and eIF3l; eIF3d depletion affects only eIF3d. They show that eIF3dKD and eIF3eKD strongly reduce proliferation and translation initiation (increased 80S monosomes, decreased polysomes), while eIF3hKD has only moderate effects.
results.evaluation: Reviewers accept these characterizations as valid. Reviewer 3 notes the authors 'use ribosome profiling of well-characterized mutants lacking subunits of eIF3.' Reviewer 2 acknowledges 'eIF3d/eKD share multiple dysregulated transcripts, perhaps due to both subcomplexes lacking eIF3d.' No methodological concerns are raised about the knockdown validation or phenotypic characterization.

results.result: The authors report that considerably more DTEGs were identified in eIF3dKD than eIF3eKD despite substantial overlap, correlating with more severe growth phenotype. They propose that eIF3d may remain partially operational even in eIF3eKD, and that common phenotypes likely result from reduced eIF3d protein levels.
results.evaluation: Reviewer 2 explicitly identifies this as a weakness: 'The differences between eIF3e and eIF3d knockdown are difficult to reconcile, especially since eIF3e knockdown leads to reduction in eIF3d levels.' This indicates the reviewers find the explanation for differential effects between eIF3dKD and eIF3eKD inadequate, though they do not reject the observations themselves.

results.result: The authors report quality control metrics for Ribo-seq libraries showing similar read length distribution (30-32 nt peak), expected 3 nt periodicity in coding sequences, and enrichment for CDS reads. PCA analysis shows NT and eIF3hKD samples cluster together while eIF3eKD and eIF3dKD cluster separately.
results.evaluation: The editor states the study uses 'convincing methods, data, and analyses.' Reviewer 3 notes 'The authors have provided a comprehensive set of data to analyze RNA and ribosome footprinting.' No concerns are raised about the technical quality of the Ribo-seq data or analysis.

results.result: The authors report that non-TOP mTORC1-sensitive transcripts and mRNAs dependent on phospho-eIF4E were predominantly translationally offset (buffered) in eIF3dKD and eIF3eKD, leading them to conclude that mTOR does not generally operate via eIF3 and eIF3 does not require mTOR activation to fine-tune ribosome protein production.
results.evaluation: Reviewers do not challenge these findings. The observations about translational buffering and independence from mTOR signaling are presented as data-driven conclusions without reviewer objection. The editor's statement about 'convincing methods, data, and analyses' implicitly supports these technical findings.

results.result: The authors report that effects of DAP5 depletion on the translatome were comparable to eIF3d-depleted cells, and since similar effects were observed with eIF3eKD and eIF3hKD, they conclude that the DAP5-dependent mechanism may rely on the entire eIF3 complex, not only eIF3d.
results.evaluation: Reviewers do not challenge this finding. While Reviewer 2 notes 'The paper would be strengthened by experiments directly testing what RNA determinants allow for transcript-specific translation regulation by the eIF3 complex,' this is a request for additional mechanistic detail rather than a challenge to the DAP5-related observations presented.

results.result: The authors conclude that eIF3 plays a critical role in translational regulation of specific mRNAs encoding regulatory proteins, often utilizing uORFs and/or specific secondary structures in their 5' UTRs, and that alterations in eIF3 subunit stoichiometry have distinct effects on the translatome affecting factors involved in cancer biology.
results.evaluation: The editor states 'the physiological significance of the gene expression changes that were observed is not clear,' directly questioning the broader biological interpretation. Reviewer 1 notes 'The authors could have explored in more detail some of their novel observations, as well as their impact on cell behavior.' Reviewer 3 states 'The paper would be strengthened if there were a clear model tying the various effects together or linking individual subunit knockdown to cancerous phenotypes.' These comments indicate uncertainty about the physiological and pathological significance of the findings.

comparisons.comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C37-C43. Both evaluations find the knockdown characterization well-supported by qPCR, western blotting, polysome profiling, and growth curves. No concerns raised by either evaluation.
Perfect agreement on claims C92-C93. Both evaluations support the DAP5-related findings showing similar effects across eIF3 knockdowns. Peer reviewers do not challenge these observations.

Both evaluations express uncertainty about claims C100-C104. OpenEval marks C103-C104 as hypotheses lacking experimental validation. Peer Reviewer 2 explicitly identifies difficulty reconciling differences between eIF3e and eIF3d knockdown, finding the explanation inadequate.

Strong agreement on claims C78-C80, C106 regarding MAPK pathway activation. Both evaluations find the evidence compelling. Peer reviewers explicitly acknowledge this as a key contribution with elevated ERK/c-Jun phosphorylation despite protein downregulation.

Agreement on claims C57-C59 regarding lysosomal and ER protein pathway enrichment. Both evaluations support the KEGG enrichment findings. Peer reviewers acknowledge increased TE of lysosomal and ER transcripts without methodological concerns.

Agreement on claims C61-C66 regarding ribosomal protein production and TOP mRNA translation. Both evaluations support the findings. Peer reviewers confirm upregulation of TOP mRNAs and ribosomal proteins, extending previous reports on eIF3d/e control of 5'TOP translation.

Agreement on claims C44-C51 regarding Ribo-seq quality metrics and differential expression analysis. Both evaluations find the technical approach convincing. Peer reviewers note 'convincing methods, data, and analyses' and accept the overlap patterns between eIF3d/e knockdowns.

Agreement on claims C44-C46 regarding Ribo-seq data quality. Both evaluations support the technical rigor. Peer reviewers provide comprehensive validation of RNA and ribosome footprinting data quality.

Agreement on claims C52-C55 regarding Venn diagram overlap patterns. Both evaluations support these findings. Peer reviewers accept the shared dysregulated transcripts between eIF3d/e knockdowns without challenge.

Agreement on claims C83-C87 regarding ISR pathway and reinitiation. Both evaluations support the findings on ATF4 and MDM2. Peer reviewers confirm this as important confirmatory work, though note lack of additional experimental evidence for Raf-1 uORF dependence.
